texts: Why did the thread harvest at the Middle Row fall on day 17 of Year 1?

fields.sentence: Why did the thread harvest at the Middle Row fall on day 17 of Year 1?

q1_issues.issue: "fall on day 17 of Year 1" is the calendar-placement idiom stating when the harvest took place, but the query reifies a separate literal fall eventuality with the harvest as its Theme and hangs the date terms on that fall event instead of on the harvest event-noun witness, so the pattern asks about a falling rather than about the harvest's date.

The noun-attached locative "at the Middle Row" is encoded with the event-oblique head Location on the harvest referent, which the same query otherwise treats as an ordinary entity filling a Theme slot; Where a THING is bars Location on an entity and routes containment "at" to the entity-side head.

q2_gaps: the calendar idiom "<event-noun> falls on <date>" — Time's light-verb-over-event-noun rule names only occurred / happened / took place, so nothing in the instruction set decides between dating the event-noun directly and reifying a literal or scalar-change fall event
review.notes: "Middle Row" correctly gets Name binding (the capitalized run exceeds the bare class word) with no invented kind atom, and (Day 17) / (Year 1) are the right structured granularity terms. The two issues above are the same underlying indecision about whether thread_harvest is an eventuality or an entity.

issues.reason: "fall on <date>" is calendar placement, not an eventuality — the literal reading is incoherent for a harvest, so the idiom coherence test of Compound concepts rules it out, and Time's light-verb-over-event-noun rule makes the event-noun's own witness the eventuality that carries the tense and Time terms; reifying a separate fall with the harvest as Theme and hanging (Day 17) / (Year 1) on it asks the reason for a falling rather than for the harvest's date.

A harvest is an event-denoting noun whose witness IS an eventuality (Time, light verbs over event-nouns: "the show" / "the storm" take time relations directly), so the event oblique Location is the correct head and "never Location on an entity" does not reach it — the issue also contradicts issue 0, which insists the harvest be treated as the eventuality.

gaps_confirmed: Time's light-verb-over-event-noun rule names only occurred / happened / took place, so the calendar idiom "<event-noun> falls on <date>" is not explicitly routed — the coherence test rules out the literal fall, but the dating rule has to be carried over to "fall on" by analogy
new_gaps: a locative PP on an event-denoting noun ("the thread harvest at the Middle Row") has no explicit routing: Where a THING is bars Location on an entity and gives LocatedIn / surface-preposition heads for things, but the instruction set never states that an event-noun's own locative takes the event-side Location — the indecision that produced issue 1
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant query drops the literal fall event and dates the harvest witness directly: (: $prf (And (Member $h thread_harvest) (Location $h $m) (Name $m "Middle Row") (Past $h) (Time $h (Day 17)) (Time $h (Year 1)) (ReasonFor $r $h)) $tv).
adjudication.notes: The structured terms (Day 17) / (Year 1), the Name binding of "Middle Row" with no invented kind atom, and the single ReasonFor line are all right and survive into the compliant form.
